Hi Hiro,

Thanks for the intro call last week. Procurement asked us to get clarity on a few items before we go to legal:

- Who is the seller-of-record on the marketplace? We need to understand whether Redwood will be the seller (invoicing customers directly) or whether CloudMart will resell Redwood and be the billing entity.
- How do taxes (VAT/state sales tax) get handled in each case — will tax be passed through to the reseller, or absorbed by the seller-of-record?
- For pass-through cases, can we get an explicit contractual liability carveout and an invoice trail suitable for our auditors?

I attached the CloudMart draft Order Form (Cloudmart_Draft_OrderForm_v3.pdf) with comments on the pass-through section. High level: procurement prefers CloudMart remain seller-of-record if possible, but they need a clear paper trail and indemnity allocation.

Can you loop in your legal and marketplace ops so we can align on redlines and a proposed mutual action plan?

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30 min call this week if that helps.

Best,

Hi all —

Thanks, Hiro. I reviewed the attached Order Form and drafted a short set of redline options (attached: redlines_marked.docx). High-level summary:

Option A — Redwood as seller-of-record
- Redwood invoices end customers; Redwood accepts tax collection/remittance (we recommend for shorter time-to-market).
- CloudMart receives reseller margin via separate settlement schedule.
- Indemnity: standard carveout for taxes retained by Redwood; reseller remains responsible for its own resale taxes.

Option B — CloudMart as reseller (CloudMart seller-of-record) [Procurement preferred]
- CloudMart invoices customers and collects/remits taxes.
- Redwood issues an invoice to CloudMart net of marketplace fees.
- Contract language required: explicit pass-through of tax liabilities to CloudMart, an audit trail requirement (line-item invoices, metering export), and a mutual indemnity bucket limited to willful misconduct.

Option C — Intermediated billing with escrow/settlement (hybrid)
- Platform collects on behalf of CloudMart, funds flow through a settlement account; tax responsibility documented in Order Form.
- Requires a ~2 week ops onboarding and verification of KYC for settlement accounts.

Redline notes (examples from the doc):
- Section 4.2 (Taxes): Replace "Redwood shall be responsible for tax collection" with "Seller-of-record will be designated in the Order Form; purchaser will rely on Seller-of-record for tax remittance unless otherwise agreed."
- New Section: "Pass-through Taxes": "When Reseller is designated as Seller-of-record, Customer shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Redwood for any taxes, interest, and penalties assessed against Redwood that arise from Reseller's failure to collect or remit taxes, except to the extent Redwood's acts or omissions materially contributed to such assessment."
- Audit trail requirement: Redwood to provide CSV metering export, invoice line-itemization, and a 12-month retention of invoice/settlement logs.

Marissa (Legal) recommends Option B only if CloudMart confirms it can accept the tax liability and provide the requested audit trail sample. If not, Option A is lower risk commercially.

I attached the redlines file with tracked changes and a short playbook of suggested language. Happy to walk through line-by-line on the call.

—Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Elena — quick operational notes from Marketplace Ops: 

- We can produce a daily line-item export (CSV) that shows order id, SKU, list price, marketplace fee, reseller net, tax collected. This export is available via secure S3 for 12 months by default; longer retention can be arranged for a fee.
- If CloudMart is seller-of-record (Option B), we will issue settlement reports to CloudMart's billing contact and net funds to the designated settlement account on a 14-day cadence.
- For escrow/intermediated flow (Option C), we need at minimum: settlement account details, KYC docs, and a two-week setup window to validate banking.
- Billing codes: please confirm whether you require consolidated invoices per month or per-transaction line items. Consolidated invoices require grouping logic we can enable but it impacts reconciliation timelines.

Action items:
1) Elena/procurement: confirm preferred seller-of-record option and required invoice granularity.
2) CloudMart billing contact to send KYC if Option C is chosen.
3) We will produce a sample CSV extract (sanitized) for your auditors within 48 hours upon request.

On the sync call we'll walk through the layout of the CSV and the fields available for audit.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Head of Marketplace Ops, Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — good options and clear detail. Procurement and legal at CloudMart reviewed the three choices and procurement confirms they are willing to be seller-of-record (Option B) subject to two confirmations:

1) Redwood provides the daily CSV export with line-item detail and 12 months retention (we understand longer retention may be a service add-on).
2) Contract language explicitly passes tax liability to CloudMart with the indemnity language Marissa proposed, and Redwood confirms Redwood will not be liable for CloudMart's failure to remit taxes except in cases of Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct.

If you can provide a DocuSign-ready Order Form with those redlines, procurement will circulate for signature. Our procurement contact is procurement@cloudmart.com — cc'd.

We prefer consolidated monthly invoices with transaction-level CSV for reconciliation (i.e., one invoice per month, plus the CSV for matching).

Please send the updated Order Form and a DocuSign link and we'll target signature next week. Happy to join the Thu sync if you prefer to walk through the CSV layout live.

Best,
Elena
